2607.06125.title: Evaluating Fine-Tuning and Metrics for Neural Decompilation of Dart AOT Binaries
2607.06125.paper_summary: Neural decompilation is increasingly studied as a code-generation problem, yet its evaluation methodology remains underdeveloped for modern languages. We present a systematic empirical study of fine-tuning effectiveness and metric validity for Dart Ahead-of-Time (AOT) neural decompilation. We evaluate six fine-tuned model variants across three base architectures (4B-8B parameters) using three metrics: CodeBLEU, compile@k, and pass@k on a new 154-task HumanEval-Dart benchmark. Our study yields three principal findings grounded in paired task-level statistical tests. First, no fine-tuning configuration produces a statistically significant pass@k improvement. The sole positive case yields +0.71 pp (McNemar p=0.21), while fine-tuning the strongest base (Qwen3-8B) causes a highly significant regression of -5.65 pp (p<0.001). This capacity-dependent trend is consistent across architectures but needs broader scale sweeps. Second, cross-lingual interference from Swift training is highly significant at 4B (-2.66 pp, p<0.001) but statistically indistinguishable from zero at 8B, consistent with the scaling hypothesis. Third, we demonstrate metric divergence: CodeBLEU and compile@k can improve significantly while pass@k moves in the opposite direction. This has implications for any LLM code generation task where fine-tuning targets superficial similarity. Error analysis reveals assembly sequence length is the strongest predictor of task difficulty (p=0.001), with a capability cliff at 200 instructions. We contribute the HumanEval-Dart benchmark, a Dart-adapted CodeBLEU, and empirical evidence that pass@k must be the primary evaluation metric for neural decompilation.
2607.06125.paper_summary_zh: 神經反編譯越來越多地被研究作為一個代碼生成問題，但其評估方法對於現代語言仍然不夠成熟。<lb/>我們提出了一項系統的實證研究，探討Dart即時（AOT）神經反編譯的微調效果和指標有效性。<lb/>我們在一個新的154任務HumanEval-Dart基準上，使用三個指標：CodeBLEU、compile@k和pass@k，評估了三種基礎架構（4B-8B參數）下的六個微調模型變體。<lb/>我們的研究得出了三個主要發現，基於配對任務級別的統計測試。<lb/>首先，沒有任何微調配置產生統計上顯著的pass@k改善。<lb/>唯一的正面案例帶來了+0.71 pp（McNemar p=0.21），而微調最強的基礎模型（Qwen3-8B）則導致了非常顯著的回歸，為-5.65 pp（p<0.001）。<lb/>這一依賴於能力的趨勢在各架構中是一致的，但需要更廣泛的範圍掃描。<lb/>其次，來自Swift訓練的跨語言干擾在4B中非常顯著（-2.66 pp，p<0.001），但在8B中與零統計上無法區分，這與比例假設一致。<lb/>第三，我們展示了指標的差異：CodeBLEU和compile@k可以顯著改善，而pass@k則朝相反方向移動。<lb/>這對於任何LLM代碼生成任務都有影響，尤其是當微調目標是表面相似性時。<lb/>錯誤分析顯示，組合序列長度是任務難度的最強預測因子（p=0.001），在200條指令處存在能力懸崖。<lb/>我們貢獻了HumanEval-Dart基準、一個Dart適配的CodeBLEU，以及實證證據表明pass@k必須是神經反編譯的主要評估指標。
